info.title: nim-proxy dashboard API
info.description:
The operator surface of nim-proxy: the settings store, user and key management, and the metrics history the dashboard renders. This document is generated from the handlers; regenerate it with `UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test --test openapi`.

Not covered: the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` passthrough (that contract is the upstream's, not nim-proxy's), the HTML page routes, the form-encoded `/login` and `/logout` browser flow, plain-text `/health`, and the Prometheus exposition at `/metrics`.

get.summary:
`GET /api/config` — the Settings page's data source, filtered by role
BEFORE serialization: a user-role response simply contains no server
settings and no other users' key rows, so DOM tampering reveals nothing.

200.description: Settings visible to the caller's role

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Window start, unix seconds. Defaults to `to - default_window_days`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Window end, unix seconds. Omitting it means "follow now".

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Rollup buckets, clamped to 2..=1000. Defaults to 288.

200.description: Live registry values plus the configuration they were sampled under
Installed locales and the server default

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/account` — change the caller's password or locale preference.
Password changes always re-verify the current password and return a fresh
cookie; locale changes preserve the existing session.

200.description: Password changed with a fresh session cookie and other sessions invalidated, or locale preference applied without changing the session.

400.description: Request failed with weak_password, invalid_action, invalid_locale, locale_not_installed, or invalid_config

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

409.description: An admin reset the password while this request was in flight; the reset wins

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/clients` — client-key create/revoke for any role
(own keys; admins revoke any); the open/keyed mode toggle is admin-only.
A created secret is returned exactly once and stored only as a digest.

200.description: Applied. On `add`, `secret` is the plaintext key — the only time it is ever served.

400.description: No such client key, more than one action, or an unknown mode

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

403.description: Revoking someone else's key, or a non-admin changing the mode

post.summary: `POST /api/settings/governor` (admin) — the per-model concurrency gate: the adaptive switch and operator-pinned caps. Fields are independent; omitted ones are left alone.

200.description: Applied, persisted, and swapped into the live runtime config

400.description: The store validator rejected the result

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

422.description: A field is missing or the wrong type — a partial body is never a silent reset

post.summary: `POST /api/settings/history` (admin) — retention plus the dashboard's default window and SLO target. Shrinking retention prunes on disk.

200.description: Applied, persisted, and swapped into the live runtime config

400.description: The store validator rejected the result

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

422.description: A field is missing or the wrong type — a partial body is never a silent reset

post.summary: `POST /api/settings/limits` (admin) — patience, timeouts and the in-flight cap. Every field is required.

200.description: Applied, persisted, and swapped into the live runtime config

400.description: The store validator rejected the result

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

422.description: A field is missing or the wrong type — a partial body is never a silent reset

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/locale` — change the persisted server default. Admin
and superuser roles share the existing server-settings authority.

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/nim-keys` — any role may add keys (owner = caller)
and manage their OWN keys; admins manage any key. The superuser's last
enabled key is protected by `validate` (the pool-floor invariant).

200.description: Applied; the pool was rebuilt with rate-state carryover

400.description: No such key, more than one action, or a store the validator rejects (e.g. removing the pool floor)

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

403.description: Not the key's owner and not an admin

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/upstream` (admin) — also flushes the model-catalog
cache and the per-model no-inject memory, which are upstream-specific.

200.description: Applied; the model catalog cache and the per-model no-inject memory were flushed

400.description: Not an http(s) URL, or a link-local address

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/users` (admin) — create/delete users, reset
passwords, change roles. Deleting a user pulls their NIM keys from the
pool and revokes their client keys — their harnesses stop; that's the
point. The superuser can never be deleted or demoted.

400.description: Weak password, unknown user, bad role, or more than one action

401.description: No session, or the caller's user was deleted

403.description: Not an admin, or a write against the superuser (undeletable, immutable role, password only via /account)

post.summary:
`POST /api/settings/validate-key` — authenticated twin of the setup
probe. The upstream is ALWAYS the configured `base_url`, never a
caller-supplied one: a request-supplied target would let any logged-in
user turn the proxy into an SSRF probe of internal hosts (the response
distinguishes reachable/rejected/unreachable). An admin testing a new
upstream saves it first, then validates. `req.base_url` is ignored.

200.description: Probe finished against the CONFIGURED upstream; any `base_url` in the body is ignored (SSRF guard)

post.summary:
`POST /setup` — one atomic claim: create the superuser, record the
initial NIM keys, persist, and mint a session. No half-configured server
state exists at any point; an abandoned wizard leaves nothing behind.

200.description: Claimed. Sets the session cookie; `client_key` carries the minted secret, which is never retrievable again.

400.description: Weak password or a config the store rejects

409.description: Setup is already complete or another caller claimed the proxy first

post.summary:
`POST /setup/validate-key` — pre-auth key probe for the wizard, bounded
by the shared login throttle plus a fixed delay (probe abuse control).

200.description: Probe finished; `ok` says whether the key worked

429.description: Probe throttle (shared with the login throttle)

rpm.description:
Requests per minute for this key's lane; defaults to 40 (NIM's free
tier).

ApiError.description:
The single error envelope every JSON endpoint answers failures with —
the same shape `/v1` uses, so one client-side branch handles both.

message.description: Operator-facing explanation; safe to show in the UI.

type.description: Always `proxy_error` — the error came from nim-proxy, not upstream.

ClientKeyRow.description:
A stored client key. The secret itself is never served back — only the
masked tail kept for display.

mode.description: `open` or `keyed` — whether `/v1` requires a client key (admin only).

remove.description: Name of the client key to revoke.

ClientsResponse.description:
`POST /api/settings/clients`. `secret` appears only on `add`, and only
this once — the store keeps a SHA-256 digest, never the secret.

ConfigResponse.description:
The Settings page's data source. `server` and `users` are absent — not
null — for non-admin callers: the filtering happens before serialization,
so DOM tampering reveals nothing.

server.description: Admin-only; omitted entirely for the `user` role.

users.description: Admin-only; omitted entirely for the `user` role.

DashboardNowResponse.description:
The "Now" strip: live registry values plus the configuration they were
sampled under. Deliberately not a slice of history — it is this instant.

auth.description: True when `/v1` requires a client key (keyed mode).

tail.description: Counters accumulated since the last persisted sample.

DashboardResponse.description:
Rolled-up history for one analytical window. `config_revision` and
`history_revision` let the dashboard skip a redraw when nothing moved.

latest.description: Latest value of each gauge in the window.

totals.description: Counter deltas summed across the window.

DashboardWindow.description:
What was asked for, what could be served, and what exists on disk —
kept separate so the UI can say "you asked for 30d, I have 3d".

following_now.description: True when the caller sent no `to`, i.e. the window tracks now.

overrides.description:
Operator-pinned per-model concurrency caps. Ordered (not a `HashMap`)
so both `config.json` and `/api/config` serialize deterministically —
a hash-ordered map made two saves of the same config differ.

cap.description: Max in-flight requests for this model, 1-10000.

remove_override.description: Model id whose pinned cap to drop.

days.description:
Retention in days; 0 = keep forever. Must be 0 or >= the default
window.

HistorySettings.description: Retention setting plus the live state of the history file.

Limits.description:
Fields are declared in ASCII order because this struct is served verbatim
inside `/api/config`, where declaration order is the wire order — see the
module docs in `src/api.rs`.

LimitsReq.description:
Mirror of `config::Limits` WITHOUT serde defaults: a partial body is a
422, never a silent reset of the omitted fields.

LocaleBootstrap.description:
Public startup data: the installed presentation locales and the
persisted server default.

MetricValue.description:
One metric series at one instant. Fields are declared in ASCII order:
this type is served inside `/api/dashboard`, where declaration order is
the wire order — see the module docs in `src/api.rs`.

Mode.description:
Whether `/v1` requires a client API key. `Keyed` with zero keys rejects
everything — fail closed; the dashboard prompts to create a key.

NimKeyRow.description:
A stored NIM key plus its live lane state. `lane`, `in_window` and
`cooldown_ms` are null for a disabled key (it holds no lane).

fingerprint.description: First 8 hex chars of SHA-256(key) — the key's public identifier.

guarded.description:
True for the superuser's only enabled key: the pool floor, which
`config::validate` refuses to remove or disable.

remove.description: Fingerprint of the key to remove.

OkResponse.description:
A settings write that applied. Success carries no data: the dashboard
re-reads `/api/config` rather than trusting an echo.

ok.description: Always `true`; failures are an [`ApiError`] with a 4xx status.

PoolSummary.description: Pool aggregate — visible to every role, since it carries no ownership.

oneOf.description: Absent for a bucket sampled before capacity was recorded.

ServerSettings.description: Admin-only server settings, mirroring the stored config sections.

oneOf.description:
Mint a first client key with the claim (the wizard sends this by
default) so a fresh keyed-mode proxy can serve /v1 immediately.

SetupResponse.description:
The first-run claim. `client_key` is present when the wizard asked for a
first client key — the one and only time that secret leaves the server.

base_url.description:
`http(s)://host[:port]`; link-local addresses are refused (cloud
metadata endpoints have no legitimate NIM use).

UserRow.description: A user row with how much of the pool they own.

remove.description:
Username to delete. Their NIM keys leave the pool and their client
keys are revoked.

base_url.description:
Only honored by `/setup/validate-key` (pre-claim, no upstream is
configured yet). The authenticated twin ignores it — see
[`validate_key`].

basic_auth.description: Dashboard username and password, for non-browser clients such as a Prometheus scraper. `Authorization: Bearer <user>:<password>` is accepted equivalently.

session_cookie.name: nimproxy_session
session_cookie.description: HMAC-signed session cookie minted by POST /login. The signing key is regenerated every boot, so a restart invalidates all sessions.

tags.name: dashboard
tags.description: Read-only telemetry the operator console renders.

tags.name: settings
tags.description: The config store's only writers. Every write is validate -> persist -> swap; a failed disk write applies nothing.

tags.name: setup
tags.description: First-run claim. **Unauthenticated** — these routes sit outside the session guard because no user exists yet. They answer 404 the moment a superuser exists, so the window is exactly one claim wide.
